title: Noor and the Passage
premise: Salvage diver Ulyana Nakamura is hired to recover equipment from a wreck the navy officially denies, only to find the government survey team that vanished there alive but changed — their memories rewritten by a resonance phenomenon in the mountain pass they were mapping. The 'Passage' is a geological anomaly that stores and rewrites human memory, and a defense contractor wants it weaponized before the monsoon seals the range. Ulyana, who measures life in miles because her own past was erased in an accident she cannot remember, must lead the broken team across the range ahead of the snows while deciding whether destroying the Passage means losing the only chance to recover who she was. In the end she collapses the Passage with the contractor's own charges, choosing the self she has built over the self she lost, and walks out of the mountains as the monsoon breaks.
about_author: J. M. Hartwell is a former maritime surveyor who spent six years working salvage contracts across the Indian Ocean before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people whose professions demand precision and whose lives refuse to cooperate with it.

chapters.title: Twelve Miles Down
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A routine deep salvage on a wrecked naval vessel introduces her meticulous, mileage-counting worldview and her partner Devi. She recovers a sealed case stamped with a contractor's logo instead of navy markings. Beat: competence masking a hollow core.

chapters.title: The Wreck That Isn't
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The manifest lists the wreck as decommissioned; the cargo says otherwise. A navy launch warns them off with unusual menace. Ulyana logs coordinates she shouldn't keep. Beat: first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Hired by Silence
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. A fixer offers triple rate to retrieve 'survey equipment' from a government team lost near the Kharang Pass. The contract forbids questions and includes a clause about 'cognitive hazards' neither of them understands. Beat: greed and need outweigh instinct.

chapters.title: The Road to Basecamp
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The trek into the foothills establishes the team's dynamics: skeptical guide Tsering, nervous comms tech Okafor, and the fixer's silent escort. Weather reports show an early monsoon building over the coast. Beat: uneasy camaraderie.

chapters.title: Gear Without Tracks
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. They find the survey camp intact — food warm, radios charged, every person gone. Footprints end mid-stride at the treeline. Okafor's instruments register a low rhythmic pulse from up-valley. Beat: dread arrives before danger does.

chapters.title: What the Pulse Does
chapters.summary: Tsering's POV. The guide reveals local stories of the 'singing stone' his grandmother forbade him to approach. Overnight, Okafor describes a childhood memory Tsering realizes belongs to someone else. Beat: the horror becomes intimate.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Near the pass mouth they find the missing survey team — alive, healthy, and serene, unable to say their own names but able to describe Ulyana's drowned childhood in perfect detail. Beat: recognition without identity.

chapters.title: The Contractor Arrives
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Voss, the contractor's site chief, lands by helicopter with armed escorts and demolition gear, claiming rescue jurisdiction. He needs the Passage mapped and contained before the monsoon grounds aircraft. Beat: the true stakes surface.

chapters.title: Miles as Memory
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Flashback interleave: the diving accident twelve years ago, the coma, the blank years. She realizes the Passage didn't just erase the survey team — it offered them better lives than the ones they had. Beat: temptation takes root.

chapters.title: Voss's Ledger
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Intercepting contractor transmissions, Okafor learns Voss plans to harvest the resonance for memory-editing technology — and that the 'rescue' contract was bait to supply test subjects. Beat: betrayal crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Ascent Begins
chapters.summary: Tsering's POV. Racing the snowline, the group starts up the pass with two of the blank survey team in tow. Rockfall, thin air, and Voss's men shadowing them. Beat: commitment — no way back down.

chapters.title: Storm Window
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A satellite call gives them forty hours before the monsoon makes landfall and closes the pass for the season. Voss offers Ulyana her missing memories on a drive if she delivers the team to him. Beat: the offer that splits her.

chapters.title: Devi's Bargain
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Devi secretly negotiates with Voss to spare Ulyana, believing the memories will destroy her. His guilt poisons the trust between partners. Beat: love weaponized into deception.

chapters.title: The Singing Stone
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the Passage's heart, a chamber where the rock hums with stored lives. Ulyana touches it and experiences fragments of her erased years — including evidence her accident was no accident. Beat: revelation and vertigo.

chapters.title: Whose Life Is This
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. One blank survey team member, given a taste of her old memories, rejects them violently, insisting she is her new self. The group fractures over whether restoration is mercy or erasure. Beat: theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Snowline Crossing
chapters.summary: Tsering's POV. The storm front arrives early. A whiteout crossing costs them supplies and nearly Okafor. Voss's team, better equipped, overtakes them on the glacier. Beat: nature as indifferent antagonist.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Col
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Voss takes the group at the high col, demanding the Passage's access codes recovered from the survey team's leader. Devi confesses his bargain to Ulyana under gunpoint. Beat: trust shattered at altitude.

chapters.title: The Drive
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Holding her stolen past in her hands, Ulyana reads enough to learn Voss engineered her original accident to recruit divers with no ties. She chooses not to load the drive. Beat: identity claimed, not recovered.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Tsering's alternating POV. Using Voss's own demolition charges, they breach the resonance chamber as the monsoon's first wall of rain hits the range. The hum dies; the blanks collapse weeping, remembering everything. Beat: climax — destruction as liberation.

chapters.title: Descent in the Rain
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. The retreat down the flooded pass, Voss's operation unraveling behind them, his helicopter grounded by weather he can't buy off. Devi carries Okafor; forgiveness is offered but not yet accepted. Beat: penance in motion.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Weeks later, back on the water, Ulyana dives the original wreck one last time and leaves the unopened drive in the deep. She stops counting miles. Beat: quiet resolution.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Ensemble close, Ulyana's final voice. Monsoon season ends; the survivors scatter — Okafor to testify, Tsering home, the restored team rebuilding lives twice-lived. Ulyana signs on to a new survey, her own this time. Beat: forward motion, self-authored.
